# 2026 US Midterms (Nov 3, 2026): Political-Science Themes and Context for the "Critical Lens" Layer

Research date: November 8, 2026. All figures are preliminary; counts were still underway in several races at the time of retrieval. "AP Voter Poll" is the name AP/PBS used in 2026 coverage for the survey formerly branded AP VoteCast (conducted by SSRS; ~80,000 voters; Oct 19/22–Nov 3; margin of error ±0.6 pts for the full sample) — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms).

**Name discrepancy flag (applies throughout):** Three separately retrieved sources (TIME, Chief Healthcare Executive, PBS/AP) name Annie Andrews's defeated South Carolina opponent as "Sen. Darline Graham." The long-serving SC senator up in 2026 under pre-election knowledge was Lindsey Graham. The site should verify the spelling against AP's results page before publishing; I have reproduced what the sources say.

---

## 1. Physicians in office ("Doctor Caucus" / "Healer Caucus")

### Takeaway
All four named physician-candidates won: Acton (OH governor), El-Sayed (MI Senate), Andrews (SC Senate), Hamawy (NJ-12, projected). The outgoing 119th Congress had 20 physicians (a tied record); reporting says the 120th "looks like it will have even more," but no outlet I could retrieve had published a final count or party split as of Nov 8.

### Cited Findings
- Annie Andrews (D, pediatrician) won the SC Senate race, defeating the Republican incumbent (named "Darline Graham" in source); her win "helped Democrats regain the Senate majority, CNN projected" — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress); same opponent name in [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/doctors-scientists-won-2026-midterm-elections/)
- Abdul El-Sayed (D) won the Michigan Senate seat over Mike Rogers; he will be the first Muslim elected to the Senate — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress); [Asian Journal](https://asianjournal.com/usa/lasvegas/becerra-ford-make-history-in-california-and-nevada/)
- Credential nuance: Chief Healthcare Executive labels El-Sayed an "epidemiologist" (not a physician); TIME calls him "Dr." and says he withdrew his residency application to pursue public health, without stating his degree — [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/doctors-scientists-won-2026-midterm-elections/). (From training data, not retrieved now: El-Sayed holds an MD and a DPhil; he never completed residency/licensure. Verify before calling him a "physician.")
- Amy Acton (D, labeled pediatrician by Chief Healthcare Executive) won Ohio governor over Vivek Ramaswamy; she became known as Ohio's health director during COVID briefings — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress); [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/doctors-scientists-won-2026-midterm-elections/). Ohio also elected its first woman governor — [Asian Journal](https://asianjournal.com/usa/lasvegas/becerra-ford-make-history-in-california-and-nevada/)
- Adam Hamawy (D, plastic and reconstructive surgeon) won NJ-12 (projected) — [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/doctors-scientists-won-2026-midterm-elections/); [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress)
- Other physician results in the provisional roundup: Richard Pan (D, pediatrician, CA-6) won; Rich McCormick (R, GA-7) won; John Cowan (R, neurosurgeon, GA-11) won (projected); Amish Shah (D, AZ) leading, uncalled; Josh Green (D, HI governor) leading; Sen. Roger Marshall (R, KS, obstetrician) lost to Adam Hamilton; Reps. Scott DesJarlais (R-TN) trailing narrowly and Greg Murphy (R-NC) narrowly leading, both uncalled. Sens. Rand Paul and John Barrasso (both R physicians) were not on the ballot — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress)
- Count: the current Congress had 20 physicians, which "had tied a record"; the next "looks like it will have even more physicians" — no number given — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress)
- Trend framing: 314 Action recruits and backs Democratic candidates with scientific and medical backgrounds; El-Sayed's platform includes reversing Medicaid cuts — [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/doctors-scientists-won-2026-midterm-elections/). Democratic leaders talk of reversing Medicaid cuts, and analysts "see potential for restoration" — [Chief Healthcare Executive](https://www.chiefhealthcareexecutive.com/view/election-2026-doctors-who-won-and-lost-bids-for-congress)
- Further coverage exists but was not retrievable (blocked): [CIDRAP "Democratic doctors win big"](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/public-health/democratic-doctors-win-big-2026-midterm-elections); [Scientific American list](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/these-are-the-doctors-and-scientists-elected-in-the-2026-midterms/)

### Inferences
- The 2026 physician cohort marks a partisan shift: historically the GOP Doctors Caucus dominated physician membership; the 2026 new arrivals named in coverage are mostly Democrats, while at least one GOP physician senator (Marshall) lost. If Shah wins and DesJarlais loses, the Democratic share rises further. This is inference from incomplete tallies.
- Medicaid cuts are the clearest policy hook linking physician candidates to the campaign; I did not find a retrieved source explicitly tying them to the "One Big Beautiful Bill" by name.

### Gaps
- Final physician count and party split for the 120th Congress — not yet published in any source I could retrieve; several physician races uncalled.
- No retrieved source explicitly framed 2026 physician candidacies as a post-COVID trend story beyond Acton's biography.
- Verify the SC opponent's name (see flag above) and the Kansas result (Marshall losing to "Adam Hamilton") against AP.

## 2. Data centers and the grid

### Takeaway
Data centers became a measurable, bipartisan-salience campaign issue tied to electricity bills and water: $380M+ in TV ads mentioned them, Democrats outspent Republicans on the topic 3-to-1, about three-quarters of voters opposed a data center in their community, and local restrictions passed almost everywhere they were on the ballot. But only about a quarter of voters called the issue "crucial" to their vote, well below corruption and cost of living.

### Cited Findings
**Polling and salience**
- About three-quarters of voters oppose a new data center in their community (AP Voter Poll), with majorities opposed in red and blue states; about one-quarter called AI data centers "crucial" to their congressional vote — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293)
- Reuters/Ipsos (2026): 64% said building data centers rapidly is not a good thing; 77% worry they will raise electricity rates; 14% would live near one. Heatmap (Sept 2025): 44% support, 42% oppose construction — [Brookings, Aug 25, 2026](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-data-centers-are-a-top-issue-in-the-2026-midterms/)
- A September poll found 70% of Democrats and 57% of Republicans backed limiting new construction; a 2026 Dallas Fed working paper estimated data centers raised wholesale electricity prices 6.9% — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/7/how-the-us-midterm-elections-reflected-resistance-to-data-centres)
- FactCheck.org cautioned the price link is "not as simple as voters may think" — [FactCheck.org](https://www.factcheck.org/2026/10/data-centers-and-electricity-prices-its-not-as-simple-as-voters-may-think/) (not fetched; headline only)

**Spending and results**
- More than $380M in TV ads mentioned data centers (AdImpact); Democrats outspent Republicans on the topic by more than 3-to-1; of 34 called governor races, 32 winners back stronger regulation and 12 back bans or moratoriums (Data Center Watch) — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293)
- Local ballot measures: 47 referendums in 44 municipalities across 12 states (21 in Ohio); restrictions approved in 44 of 45 completed contests (Redbud Consulting) — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293). Al Jazeera counts 40 of 41 rejecting development (exception: Harwood, ND) — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/7/how-the-us-midterm-elections-reflected-resistance-to-data-centres). Counts differ by tracker.

**Ohio**
- Acton pledged to block projects that don't meet set standards; Morgan Stanley said her win "creates significant risk of data center project delays" — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293). (The word "moratorium" for Acton was not confirmed in retrieved sources; ABC describes conditional blocking.)
- Sherrod Brown (D) beat Sen. Jon Husted (R), making Husted's data-center support central; Brown's ad called Husted the "face of data centers" (Husted backed tax breaks as lieutenant governor) — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/7/how-the-us-midterm-elections-reflected-resistance-to-data-centres); [Brookings](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-data-centers-are-a-top-issue-in-the-2026-midterms/)

**Texas**
- Gina Hinojosa (D) defeated Gov. Greg Abbott; she said she would block permits that aren't a good deal or lack resident input; Morgan Stanley called her win the "most important election result" for data center development — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293). Al Jazeera describes her call as a moratorium on new approvals until stronger local protections exist — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/7/how-the-us-midterm-elections-reflected-resistance-to-data-centres). ("Caps" is not the term used in either retrieved source.)
- Abbott had called Texas "the epicenter of AI development" before moving to clamp down late; he endorsed an "audit" — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293); [Brookings](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-data-centers-are-a-top-issue-in-the-2026-midterms/)
- James Talarico (D) flipped the Senate seat pledging more regulation and closed-loop water systems; won Corpus Christi by 12 points, where the reservoir fell to 8% capacity earlier in 2026 — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/7/how-the-us-midterm-elections-reflected-resistance-to-data-centres)
- Clayton Tucker (D) won agriculture commissioner, first Democrat since 1986, citing ranchers' water concerns — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293)


**Georgia — PSC as precursor**
- 2025: Democrats Peter Hubbard and Alicia Johnson each won PSC special elections with 60%+ amid rate concerns; PSC had approved six rate hikes since 2022, froze base rates to 2028, and approved ~10 GW of new Georgia Power generation largely for data centers — [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/110426-democrats-flip-georgia-psc-as-power-bills-data-center-costs-loom)
- 2026: Democrats took PSC control (was 3-2 GOP): Hubbard 56.2% over Fitz Johnson; Sheila Edwards 55.2% over Josh Tolbert; Hubbard backs a 12–18 month data center moratorium — [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/110426-democrats-flip-georgia-psc-as-power-bills-data-center-costs-loom)

**Other states**
- Wisconsin governor-elect David Crowley (D) moved from opposing to backing a moratorium; supports ending data center sales-tax exemption — [ABC News/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/data-centers-beating-midterm-elections-reckoning-ahead-tech-137902293)
- Nevada's Aaron Ford proposed reviewing data center tax breaks and pausing new incentives — [Asian Journal](https://asianjournal.com/usa/lasvegas/becerra-ford-make-history-in-california-and-nevada/)
- Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro shifted to restrictions via executive order; New York enacted the first statewide moratorium on new hyperscale centers — [Brookings](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-data-centers-are-a-top-issue-in-the-2026-midterms/)

### Inferences
- The issue functioned as a local, concrete proxy for broader affordability and anti-tech sentiment (Brookings's "techlash" argument is analyst interpretation, not a measured finding).
- High opposition (~75%) combined with low "crucial" salience (~25%) suggests data centers shaped framing and local referendums more than they decided top-of-ticket outcomes.

### Gaps
- DeSantis's 2025–26 data-center skepticism: no retrieved source covered it.
- Virginia and Arizona 2026 specifics: not found in retrieved sources.
- Acton's exact proposal language (moratorium vs. conditional permits) not confirmed.

## 3. State vs. federal tension / sub-national federalism

### Takeaway
Democrats won at least 28 governorships (first majority since 2006), and reporting framed the governor races as a referendum on state resistance to Trump over National Guard deployments, immigration operations, aid conditions, and federal control of elections. Aaron Ford explicitly ran on suing the Trump administration; I found no retrieved statement from Becerra or Bottoms framing their wins in federalism terms.

### Cited Findings
- 36 states elected governors; 19 open; Republicans held 26 of 50 beforehand; Democrats will hold at least 28 in 2027, first majority since 2006 — [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/politics/2026/11/02/democrats-press-to-win-a-majority-of-governors-offices-in-midterms-after-power-struggles-with-trump/)
- Conflicts cited: Trump's Guard call-ups, federal immigration operations in Democratic-led states, conditions on federal aid, and Trump's push for federal control over election rules including mail voting restrictions — [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/politics/2026/11/02/democrats-press-to-win-a-majority-of-governors-offices-in-midterms-after-power-struggles-with-trump/)
- Aaron Ford (NV AG) campaigned on his record of challenging the administration in court; unseated Gov. Joe Lombardo; Nevada's first Black governor; Democrats swept all six NV statewide offices for the first time since 1962; he plans an "affordability emergency" — [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/politics/2026/11/02/democrats-press-to-win-a-majority-of-governors-offices-in-midterms-after-power-struggles-with-trump/); [Asian Journal](https://asianjournal.com/usa/lasvegas/becerra-ford-make-history-in-california-and-nevada/)
- Becerra (CA) defeated Steve Hilton; first Latino elected governor by popular vote; after winning, declined to commit to reversing Medi-Cal cuts for undocumented immigrants pending budget review — [Asian Journal](https://asianjournal.com/usa/lasvegas/becerra-ford-make-history-in-california-and-nevada/)
- Bottoms (GA) defeated Rick Jackson; her coverage centered on healthcare and history ("standing on shoulders made of steel") — [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/politics/2026/11/02/democrats-press-to-win-a-majority-of-governors-offices-in-midterms-after-power-struggles-with-trump/); [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91635793/keisha-lance-bottoms-victory-speech-fraught-georgia-history)
- Background, 2025 Guard litigation: Trump federalized California's Guard over Newsom's objection (4,000+ troops plus Marines to LA, June 2025); Oregon and Illinois sued over Portland and Chicago; federal judges issued TROs; the Supreme Court upheld the Illinois block before Christmas 2025; Trump withdrew troops from all three states on New Year's Eve "for now" — [NPR, Jan 15, 2026](https://www.npr.org/2026/01/15/nx-s1-5672596/national-guard-trump-attorney-general). Illinois AG Raoul: AGs have "each other on speed dial" — same source
- AP Voter Poll: about 7 in 10 voters said Congress is not doing enough to check the presidency, including about 4 in 10 Republicans — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms)

### Inferences
- With Congress now Democratic (see §4), the "states as counterweight" role may shift toward federal oversight; the governors' majority matters most for election administration before 2028 (AP's framing).
- Becerra's post-election hedging on Medi-Cal illustrates fiscal limits on state counter-policy after federal Medicaid cuts.

### Gaps
- Total count of Democratic AG lawsuits against the administration (Stateline and Axios pages failed to load).
- Tariff lawsuits by states: not covered in retrieved sources.
- Direct federalism quotes from Becerra or Bottoms: not found.

## 4. Coalitions, issues, turnout, and overall result

### Takeaway
A Democratic wave: Democrats won both chambers and a governors' majority, with Republicans reportedly flipping no Democratic-held seats except via redistricting. AP's poll shows young voters (~7 in 10 Democratic) and Hispanic voters (Republican share down from ~4 in 10 for Trump in 2024 to ~1 in 3) moving back to Democrats; economy (~4 in 10) and democracy (~3 in 10) led as top issues, with corruption and cost of living most often called "crucial."

### Cited Findings
**Overall result (preliminary, as of Nov 6)**
- House: D 252, R 155, 28 uncalled; prior R 220/D 215; net D +40 (source also says 42 flips — internal inconsistency) — [DemList](https://demlist.substack.com/p/demdaily-2026-election-results-the) (Democratic-aligned; verify against AP). CNN headline: Democrats "projected to win over 250 House seats" — [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/05/politics/live-news/midterm-election-congress) (not fetched)
- Senate: D 54, R 44, 2 uncalled (Alaska: Peltola 48.17% vs. Sullivan 47.88%; Mississippi: Colom 49.04% vs. Hyde-Smith 48.85%); flips to D: IA, KS, ME, NC, OH, SC, TX; prior R 53/D 47 — [DemList](https://demlist.substack.com/p/demdaily-2026-election-results-the)
- Governors: D 28, R 20, 2 uncalled (AK, KS); flips to D: GA, IA, NV, OH, TX; net D +5 (potential +6); prior D 24/R 26 — [DemList](https://demlist.substack.com/p/demdaily-2026-election-results-the); corroborated "at least 28" by [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/politics/2026/11/02/democrats-press-to-win-a-majority-of-governors-offices-in-midterms-after-power-struggles-with-trump/). (Note: Asian Journal lists Wisconsin's Crowley as governor-elect; Wisconsin was Democratic-held, so not a flip.)
- CNBC headline: "Republicans fail to flip a single seat" — [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/democrats-2026-midterm-election-results.html) (page blocked; headline only). ABC's redistricting tally shows GOP flipped TX-32 and TN-9 via new maps — see §5, so the CNBC claim likely refers to non-redistricted seats or predates those calls.

**AP Voter Poll coalitions**
- Under-30 voters: about 7 in 10 backed Democratic House candidates vs. roughly even Trump–Harris split in 2024; about 1 in 10 of the electorate — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms)
- Hispanic voters: about 6 in 10 Democratic, about one-third Republican vs. roughly 4 in 10 for Trump in 2024; about 7 in 10 say Trump's policies worsened the economy — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms)
- AP headline: Democrats "won back support from five key groups that shifted toward Trump in 2024" — [US News/AP](https://www.usnews.com/news/politics/articles/2026-11-04/democrats-won-back-support-from-five-key-groups-that-shifted-toward-trump-in-2024-the-ap-voter-poll) (not fetched; groups beyond young and Hispanic unconfirmed)
- Independents: the "vast majority" say Congress isn't checking the president enough; no vote-share figure retrieved — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms)

**Issues and Trump**
- Top issue: economy ~4 in 10; democracy ~3 in 10; immigration and healthcare ~1 in 10 each. About half called corruption and cost of living "crucial," more than immigration enforcement, the Iran war, or AI data centers — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms)
- About 6 in 10 disapprove of Trump; ~4 in 10 voted to oppose him vs. just under 2 in 10 to support; ~two-thirds say his policies worsened the economy (~8 in 10 of them voted D) — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms); [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/how-trump-and-republicans-lost-the-2026-midterm-elections-according-to-ap-voter-poll)
- About 6 in 10 were "very concerned" about grocery costs; party favorability ~half D vs. ~4 in 10 R — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/how-trump-and-republicans-lost-the-2026-midterm-elections-according-to-ap-voter-poll)

**State snapshots**
- Texas: ~2 in 10 reported "severe" inflation hardship (~three-quarters backed Talarico); ~two-thirds said Ken Paxton lacked the character to serve — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/how-trump-and-republicans-lost-the-2026-midterm-elections-according-to-ap-voter-poll). Texas early vote 7.7M+, surpassing the 2018 record — [News From The States](https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/more-77-million-texans-voted-early-2026-election-surpassing-2018-record) (headline only)
- South Carolina: ~6 in 10 said the GOP senator lacked the experience to serve (source names "Darline Graham") — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/how-trump-and-republicans-lost-the-2026-midterm-elections-according-to-ap-voter-poll)
- North Carolina: ~6 in 10 said Michael Whatley was "too supportive" of Trump — same source
- Georgia: Bottoms won; Democrats flipped the PSC (see §2). Ohio: Acton and Brown won (see §§1–2)

### Inferences
- The young and Hispanic reversals suggest 2024's shifts were contingent and anti-incumbent, not realignment (interpretive).
- Corruption and democracy as leading concerns, plus 7 in 10 wanting more congressional checks, point to an accountability-driven vote as much as an economic one.

### Gaps
- Suburban and independent vote shares vs. 2024: not in retrieved pages.
- National turnout figure: not published in retrieved sources by Nov 8.
- Final House count: 28 seats uncalled as of Nov 6.

## 5. Broader context: Iran war, fuel prices, Trump approval, redistricting

### Takeaway
The Iran war is real: US military action began Feb 28, 2026, and gas hit $4.15/gal on Election Day, the highest Election Day price on record (+~40% since February). Mid-decade redistricting backfired on Republicans: of 15 seats the GOP redrew to flip, Democrats held 11 as of Nov 5, while California's Prop 50 and Utah's new map delivered 6 Democratic flips.

### Cited Findings
- US military action against Iran began Feb 28, 2026, disrupting Strait of Hormuz traffic (recovering to 82–92% of prewar levels by late September) — [Fortune/The Conversation](https://fortune.com/2026/11/06/gas-prices-midterm-election-iran-war-incumbents)
- AAA average gas: $2.98 (Feb 2026) to $4.15 (Nov 3), the highest on any Election Day; below the June 2022 record of $4.929 — same source
- Trump approval at election: about 6 in 10 voters disapproved (AP Voter Poll) — [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-voter-poll-how-key-demographic-groups-voted-in-the-2026-midterms). The Iran war ranked below corruption and cost of living as "crucial" — same source
- Redistricting: GOP-led redraws in Texas, Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee. Of 15 targeted seats, Democrats held 11 (AL-2, FL-14, FL-22, FL-25, NC-1, OH-1, OH-9, TX-9, TX-28, TX-34, TX-35); GOP flipped TX-32 and TN-9; FL-9 and LA-6 uncalled. Democrats flipped 6 in redrawn California (CA-1, CA-3, CA-6, CA-41, CA-48) and Utah (UT-1) — [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/won-redistricting-war-democrats/story?id=137858678)
- Texas Republicans' redistricting "gamble backfires" — [Spectrum News](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/tx/dallas-fort-worth/news/2026/11/05/texas-republican-redistricting-midterms) (headline only)

### Inferences
- Gerrymanders drawn on 2024 margins proved fragile in a wave year ("dummymander" effect, analyst framing).
- The Iran war likely affected the result through gas prices more than through foreign policy as a top issue.

### Gaps
- Missouri and Virginia redistricting outcomes not covered in retrieved sources.
- Current 2026 CPI inflation rate not retrieved.
